refined_question: For the standard non-block symmetric Lanczos algorithm applied to a symmetric matrix A, possibly with a preconditioner M, suppose that matrix-vector products and/or preconditioner applications are available only through a general inexact model—for example, computed products satisfy fl(Ax)=(A+ΔA)x and computed preconditioned vectors z for residuals r satisfy (M+ΔM)z=r, without requiring an explicit formula for ΔA or ΔM. Develop a Paige-style analysis of the resulting computed Lanczos process under such general inexact-operator models, obtaining bounds or structural descriptions that either genuinely extend Paige’s finite-precision analysis or provide a simpler, more interpretable account of the algorithm’s behavior. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 2.18 exactly: the official statement on p. 18 asks to analyze Lanczos under general models of inexact matrix-vector multiplication and/or preconditioner use, with progress measured by generalizing Paige’s analysis and/or yielding easier-to-understand insight. The surrounding paragraph on the same page supplies the hidden scope that makes the problem stand-alone: Paige’s original setting is the standard floating-point model; the paper wants a more general inexact-operator model and explicitly gives representative forms for inexact matvecs and inexact preconditioner application. The immediately following text mentions the Stieltjes procedure only as one possible avenue for insight, and Problem 2.19 separately asks about block Lanczos, so the refined question should stay with standard Lanczos and should not be broadened.
